occupation_map.Ministry civil servant: Kokka Komuin (国家公務員) — retired ministry official
occupation_map.University professor: Daigaku Kyoju — university professor (Kyoto Daigaku, formerly Kyoto Teikoku Daigaku)

allowed_titles: -sensei (for academic or doctor in dialogue only)
pun_style: Subtle Japanese wordplay embedded in given names or surnames for minor witness characters — exploit homophones or kanji double-meanings (e.g., a name whose reading evokes 'saw everything' or 'heard it all'). Keep deadpan and plausible as a real Japanese name of the era. Maximum two such puns total.
notes: Era is early Showa post-Occupation Japan, 1963. Surnames precede given names in Japanese order. Occupations should reflect mid-century Japanese institutional naming. Kyoto Imperial University had been renamed Kyoto University (Kyoto Daigaku) in 1947 — the character may nostalgically reference the old name but formal setting uses the current one. Ryokan staff would use occupational terms current to the hospitality trade. Ink merchants (sumi/boku traders) were a real itinerant trade in this period. Snowfall on Kurama road adds plausible isolation. No Western honorifics in narration; -sensei acceptable in dialogue for the professor or doctor.
